scope: Read-only frozen-source and existing resource-evidence audit. No protocol changes, simulations, resource escalation, biological accuracy assessment, or challenge-answer reads.
conclusion: Ancestry-table growth and simplification workspace are a source-backed plausible explanation for the sawtooth memory burden. The exact failing allocation and required peak remain unidentified; resource feasibility is unresolved.
observations: Same-seed case5 retry used Q=1, full chromosome7 length159345973, 25 diploid samples, burn-in1, same catalog history and conditioning; scheduler and stderr confirm OOM under22GiB after1774.5612776959315 driver seconds.

Retry cgroup high-water mark reached23622320128 bytes. At1520.55s after monitoring began, current usage fell from19.3437GiB to5.6094GiB; at1690.61s it fell from18.4739GiB to5.9185GiB. These are measured aggregate cgroup drops, not identified simplification events.
Only failed status exists in retry output. SLiM failed before returning to Python, so recapitation, neutral overlay, VCF materialization, predictor and RAiSD were not running.
Frozen v4 driver and current driver differ only in downstream RAiSD peak validation/provenance; the simulation call is unchanged.
Current Betty stdpopsim engine and SLiM binary SHA256 match their frozen software manifest.

source_findings.fact: stdpopsim invokes initializeTreeSeq(timeUnit="generations") without a simplification override. SLiM4.3 defaults to target pre/post table-row ratio10, initial interval20, adaptive interval bounded1..1000. Simplification is enabled, but the policy is not a memory-cap policy.

Simplification retains ancestry of all extant diploid genomes as well as any remembered samples; final sample25 is not the live ancestral population size. Default retainCoalescentOnly is true and extinct unneeded individuals are filtered, so no intentional all-history retention was identified.

Bundled tskit simplifier allocates maps proportional to node count and copies input tables before truncating/rebuilding output tables; simplification can therefore require substantial temporary workspace above its steady table storage.

No double demographic scaling found: driver supplies untouched catalog diploid sizes and Q=1; engine handles N/Q, growth*Q and time/Q. Catalog size ranges about7156..71560; full chromosome ancestry is expected to exceed constantN10000 burden.

Engine buffers stdout/stderr using communicate(), including per-generation growth DEBUG lines at default verbosity2, but default verbosity does not enable the growing population-history dictionaries or per-mutation DEBUG3 records. No evidence establishes logs as the multi-GiB cause; the checkpoint had not yet been observed, so repeated rejection histories were not demonstrated.

Neutral mutations are added after forward simulation; only nonneutral DFE proportions enter forward mutation-rate maps. No unnecessary whole-chromosome neutral mutation population was identified in the failing forward stage.

inference.plausible_mechanism: Default ratio10 permits accumulating large unsimplified ancestry tables. Increasing inherited ancestry through the Zigzag history and temporary copy/map allocations during simplification can create rising peaks with large drops. Existing trace is consistent with this mechanism but does not prove which event killed the run.
not_established: Whether kill occurred during growth, sorting, copying or other allocation
Whether a shorter simplification interval would finish under22GiB
A finite upper memory requirement for the full history

prospective_adaptation_not_authorized_or.biological_semantics: The examined auto-simplification and simplifier paths perform deterministic ancestry bookkeeping; no RNG draws or demographic/selection changes appear there. A shorter interval is therefore a bookkeeping adaptation by source inspection, not a different biological model. It can alter internal node identifiers, ordering, provenance and possibly downstream neutral-overlay bitwise realization; exact VCF byte identity is not promised.
prospective_adaptation_not_authorized_or.first_verification: Before any chromosome retry, run a separately approved <=5min paired software fixture under the same binary with default versus interval20, identical seeded reproduction/selection, recorded sample pedigree identities, population/selected-allele trajectories and canonical marginal ancestry comparisons. Include checkpoint restore behavior. Treat as software evidence only; do not tune interval using recovery accuracy.
prospective_adaptation_not_authorized_or.resource_verification: Only after software equivalence checks and separate approval: at most one same-seed case5 bookkeeping retry within the SAME22GiB and original2h limits, with periodic tick/population logging streamed to a file and external cgroup monitoring. Preserve original OOM outcome and attempt denominator. A new OOM or timeout remains failure; no escalation or further cases assumed.
prospective_adaptation_not_authorized_or.tradeoff: Shorter intervals may lower transient table growth at additional CPU cost; neither completion nor peak reduction is guaranteed.
